data.content_ref: inline:The answer misapplies the formula 2n for n cuts through the center. For 4 concurrent lines (all passing through one point), the standard result is 2n = 8 only if 'concurrent' is misread as the maximal general-position count; but here all 4 lines share the same center point, so every line is split at the common point and the number of regions is actually 2·4 = 8 only under the 2n rule, which gives 8. However, the deeper fault is the inconsistent mechanism: it first invokes knife thickness to avoid exact concurrence, then immediately re-imposes the zero-width idealization to recover 2n=8, leaving no stable justification for why 8 rather than 6 (the concurrent degenerate case gives 2n) is privileged.
